NASB.1: Then Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned in safety to his house in Jerusalem.
NASB.2: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, 'Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD and so [bring] wrath on yourself from the LORD?
NASB.3: 'But there is [some] good in you, for you have removed the Asheroth from the land and you have set your heart to seek God.'
NASB.4: So Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem and went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
NASB.5: He appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.
NASB.6: He said to the judges, 'Consider what you are doing, for you do not judge for man but for the LORD who is with you when you render judgment.
NASB.7: 'Now then let the fear of the LORD be upon you; be very careful what you do, for the LORD our God will have no part in unrighteousness or partiality or the taking of a bribe.'
NASB.8: In Jerusalem also Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and priests, and some of the heads of the fathers' [households] of Israel, for the judgment of the LORD and to judge disputes among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
NASB.9: Then he charged them saying, 'Thus you shall do in the fear of the LORD, faithfully and wholeheartedly.
NASB.10: 'Whenever any dispute comes to you from your brethren who live in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and ordinances, you shall warn them so that they may not be guilty before the LORD, and wrath may [not] come on you and your brethren. Thus you shall do and you will not be guilty.
NASB.11: 'Behold, Amariah the chief priest will be over you in all that pertains to the LORD, and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in all that pertains to the king. Also the Levites shall be officers before you. Act resolutely, and the LORD be with the upright.'

ESV.1: Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned in safety to his house in Jerusalem.
ESV.2: But Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath has gone out against you from the LORD.
ESV.3: Nevertheless, some good is found in you, for you destroyed the Asheroth out of the land, and have set your heart to seek God.”
ESV.4: Jehoshaphat lived at Jerusalem. And he went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
ESV.5: He appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,
ESV.6: and said to the judges, “Consider what you do, for you judge not for man but for the LORD. He is with you in giving judgment.
ESV.7: Now then, let the fear of the LORD be upon you. Be careful what you do, for there is no injustice with the LORD our God, or partiality or taking bribes.”
ESV.8: Moreover, in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed certain Levites and priests and heads of families of Israel, to give judgment for the LORD and to decide disputed cases. They had their seat at Jerusalem.
ESV.9: And he charged them: “Thus you shall do in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness, and with your whole heart:
ESV.10: whenever a case comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities, concerning bloodshed, law or commandment, statutes or rules, then you shall warn them, that they may not incur guilt before the LORD and wrath may not come upon you and your brothers. Thus you shall do, and you will not incur guilt.
ESV.11: And behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the governor of the house of Judah, in all the king's matters, and the Levites will serve you as officers. Deal courageously, and may the LORD be with the upright!”

WEB.1: Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem.
WEB.2: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked, and love those who hate Yahweh? Because of this, wrath is on you from before Yahweh.

WEB.4: Jehoshaphat lived at Jerusalem; and he went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to Yahweh, the God of their fathers.
WEB.5: He set judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,
WEB.6: and said to the judges, “Consider what you do, for you don’t judge for man, but for Yahweh; and he is with you in the judgment.
WEB.7: Now therefore let the fear of Yahweh be on you. Take heed and do it; for there is no iniquity with Yahweh our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of bribes.”

NLT.1: When King Jehoshaphat of Judah arrived safely home in Jerusalem,
NLT.2: Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him. “Why should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD?” he asked the king. “Because of what you have done, the LORD is very angry with you.
NLT.3: Even so, there is some good in you, for you have removed the Asherah poles throughout the land, and you have committed yourself to seeking God.”
NLT.4: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he went out among the people, traveling from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, encouraging the people to return to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
NLT.5: He appointed judges throughout the nation in all the fortified towns,
NLT.6: and he said to them, “Always think carefully before pronouncing judgment. Remember that you do not judge to please people but to please the LORD. He will be with you when you render the verdict in each case.
NLT.7: Fear the LORD and judge with integrity, for the LORD our God does not tolerate perverted justice, partiality, or the taking of bribes.”
NLT.8: In Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and priests and clan leaders in Israel to serve as judges for cases involving the LORD’s regulations and for civil disputes.
NLT.9: These were his instructions to them: “You must always act in the fear of the LORD, with faithfulness and an undivided heart.
NLT.10: Whenever a case comes to you from fellow citizens in an outlying town, whether a murder case or some other violation of God’s laws, commands, decrees, or regulations, you must warn them not to sin against the LORD, so that he will not be angry with you and them. Do this and you will not be guilty.
NLT.11: “Amariah the high priest will have final say in all cases involving the LORD. Zebadiah son of Ishmael, a leader from the tribe of Judah, will have final say in all civil cases. The Levites will assist you in making sure that justice is served. Take courage as you fulfill your duties, and may the LORD be with those who do what is right.”

CSB17.1: King Jehoshaphat of Judah returned to his home in Jerusalem in peace.
CSB17.2: Then Jehu <sup>ⓛ</sup> son of the seer Hanani went out to confront him <sup>[1]</sup> and said to King Jehoshaphat, “Do you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? <sup>ⓜ</sup> Because of this, the LORD’s wrath is on you. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.3: However, some good is found in you, for you have eradicated the Asherah poles from the land and have decided to seek God.” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.4: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and once again he went out among the people from Beer-sheba to the hill country of Ephraim and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their ancestors. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.5: He appointed judges in all the fortified cities of the land of Judah, city by city. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.6: Then he said to the judges, “Consider what you are doing, for you do not judge for a mere mortal, but for the LORD, who is with you in the matter of judgment. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.7: And now, may the terror of the LORD be on you. Watch what you do, for there is no injustice or partiality or taking bribes with the LORD our God.” <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.8: Jehoshaphat also appointed in Jerusalem some of the Levites and priests and some of the Israelite family heads for deciding the LORD’s will and for settling disputes of the residents of <sup>[2]</sup> Jerusalem.
CSB17.9: He commanded them, saying, “In the fear of the LORD, with integrity, and wholeheartedly, you are to do the following:
CSB17.10: For every dispute that comes to you from your brothers who dwell in their cities — whether it regards differences of bloodguilt, law, commandment, statutes, or judgments <sup>ⓕ</sup>  — you are to warn them, so they will not incur guilt before the LORD and wrath will not come on you and your brothers. <sup>ⓖ</sup> Do this, and you will not incur guilt.
CSB17.11: “Note that Amariah, the chief priest, is over you in all matters related to the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in all matters related to the king, and the Levites are officers in your presence. Be strong; may the LORD be with those who do what is good.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>

AMP.1: Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned safely to his house (palace) in Jerusalem.
AMP.2: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the ungodly and love those who hate the LORD and in doing so bring wrath from the LORD on yourself?
AMP.3: But there are some good things found in you, for you have removed the Asherim (idols) from the land and you have set your heart to seek God [with all your soul's desire]."
AMP.4: So Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and he went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
AMP.5: He appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,
AMP.6: and he said to the judges, "Be careful what you do, for you do not judge for man, but for the LORD who is with you in the matter of judgment.
AMP.7: So now let the fear (reverent awe) of the LORD be on you [to keep you from making unjust decisions]; be careful in what you do, for there is no injustice with the LORD our God, or partiality, or acceptance of a bribe."
AMP.8: In Jerusalem also Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, priests, and heads of the fathers' households of Israel to render the judgment of the LORD and to judge disputes among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
AMP.9: Then the king commanded them, "Do this in the fear of the LORD, faithfully and wholeheartedly.
AMP.10: Whenever any dispute comes to you from your brothers (relatives) who live in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, or between statutes and judgments, you are to warn [and instruct] them so that they may not be guilty before the LORD; otherwise [God's] wrath will come on you and your brothers. Do this and you will not be guilty.
AMP.11: Behold, Amariah the chief priest will be over you in all matters of the LORD, and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the governor of the house of Judah, in all the king's matters; and the Levites will serve you as officers. Deal courageously, and may the LORD be with the upright."

NIV.1: When Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem,
NIV.2: Jehu the seer, the son of Hanani, went out to meet him and said to the king, “Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the Lord? Because of this, the wrath of the Lord is upon you.
NIV.3: There is, however, some good in you, for you have rid the land of the Asherah poles and have set your heart on seeking God.”
NIV.4:
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and he went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim and turned them back to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
NIV.5: He appointed judges in the land, in each of the fortified cities of Judah.
NIV.6: He told them, “Consider carefully what you do, because you are not judging for man but for the Lord, who is with you whenever you give a verdict.
NIV.7: Now let the fear of the Lord be upon you. Judge carefully, for with the Lord our God there is no injustice or partiality or bribery.”
NIV.8: In Jerusalem also, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, priests and heads of Israelite families to administer the law of the Lord and to settle disputes. And they lived in Jerusalem.
NIV.9: He gave them these orders: “You must serve faithfully and wholeheartedly in the fear of the Lord.
NIV.10: In every case that comes before you from your fellow countrymen who live in the cities—whether bloodshed or other concerns of the law, commands, decrees or ordinances—you are to warn them not to sin against the Lord; otherwise his wrath will come on you and your brothers. Do this, and you will not sin.
NIV.11: “Amariah the chief priest will be over you in any matter concerning the Lord, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the tribe of Judah, will be over you in any matter concerning the king, and the Levites will serve as officials before you. Act with courage, and may the Lord be with those who do well.”

MSG.1: But Jehoshaphat king of Judah got home safe and sound.
MSG.2: Jehu, son of Hanani the seer, confronted King Jehoshaphat: "You have no business helping evil, cozying up to God-haters. Because you did this, God is good and angry with you.
MSG.3: But you're not all bad—you made a clean sweep of the polluting sex-and-religion shrines; and you were single-minded in seeking God."
MSG.4: Jehoshaphat kept his residence in Jerusalem but made a regular round of visits among the people, from Beersheba in the south to Mount Ephraim in the north, urging them to return to God, the God of their ancestors.
MSG.5: And he was diligent in appointing judges in the land—each of the fortress cities had its judge.
MSG.6: He charged the judges: "This is serious work; do it carefully. You are not merely judging between men and women; these are God's judgments that you are passing on.
MSG.7: Live in the fear of God—be most careful, for God hates dishonesty, partiality, and bribery."
MSG.8: In Jerusalem Jehoshaphat also appointed Levites, priests, and family heads to decide on matters that had to do with worship and mediating local differences.
MSG.9: He charged them: "Do your work in the fear of God; be dependable and honest in your duties.
MSG.10: When a case comes before you involving any of your fellow citizens, whether it seems large (like murder) or small (like matters of interpretation of the law), you are responsible for warning them that they are dealing with God. Make that explicit, otherwise both you and they are going to be dealing with God's wrath. Do your work well or you'll end up being as guilty as they are.
MSG.11: "Amariah the chief priest is in charge of all cases regarding the worship of God; Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the tribe of Judah, is in charge of all civil cases; the Levites will keep order in the courts. Be bold and diligent. And God be with you as you do your best."

NET.1: When King Jehoshaphat of Judah returned home safely to Jerusalem,
NET.2: the prophet Jehu son of Hanani confronted him; he said to King Jehoshaphat, “Is it right to help the wicked and be an ally of those who oppose the LORD? Because you have done this the LORD is angry with you!
NET.3: Nevertheless you have done some good things; you removed the Asherah poles from the land and you were determined to follow the LORD.”
NET.4: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out among the people from Beer Sheba to the hill country of Ephraim and encouraged them to follow the LORD God of their ancestors.
NET.5: He appointed judges throughout the land and in each of the fortified cities of Judah.
NET.6: He told the judges, “Be careful what you do, for you are not judging for men, but for the LORD, who will be with you when you make judicial decisions.
NET.7: Respect the LORD and make careful decisions, for the LORD our God disapproves of injustice, partiality, and bribery.”
NET.8: In Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed some Levites, priests, and Israelite family leaders to judge on behalf of the LORD and to settle disputes among the residents of Jerusalem.
NET.9: He commanded them: “Carry out your duties with respect for the LORD, with honesty, and with pure motives.
NET.10: Whenever your countrymen who live in the cities bring a case before you (whether it involves a violent crime or other matters related to the law, commandments, rules, and regulations), warn them that they must not sin against the LORD. If you fail to do so, God will be angry with you and your colleagues; but if you obey, you will be free of guilt.
NET.11: You will report to Amariah the chief priest in all matters pertaining to the LORD’s law, and to Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the family of Judah, in all matters pertaining to the king. The Levites will serve as officials before you. Confidently carry out your duties! May the LORD be with those who do well!”
